headline: BNP Paribas raised its price target for Nvidia shares to $345 from $285, saying the chipmaker's complete set of AI products keeps it ahead of rivals.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a bank's price-target change reported by The Economic Times; it is one opinion, not news about Nvidia's business.
importance_line: People who hold Nvidia through share funds hear a bullish view from a large bank, but a target price is a forecast built on assumptions such as a three-quarter share of the AI computing market and gross margins above 70%.
summary: The Economic Times reports that BNP Paribas kept its "Outperform" rating (expecting the shares to beat the market) on Nvidia and raised its target price to $345 from $285, up to 47% above the $234 share price on 2 October. The bank argues that Nvidia's mix of chips, networking and software is hard for rivals to copy as AI moves to complex "inference" work (running trained models), and expects Nvidia to keep at least three-quarters of the AI computing market by value and gross margins above 70%.
notes: NDTV Profit page blocked (HTTP 403); the same note was read in The Economic Times (ETMarkets.com), whose link is used as url. Livemint relays the ET report and says it could not verify it independently. Analyst opinion.
